name: Pattern 2: The Human Review Gate
title: Pattern 2: The Human Review Gate
answer: The Human Review Gate is a limit on AI, not a use of it: certain decisions must be made by a person, with AI only informing. It matters because grades, services, discipline, placement, evaluation, safety flags, and hiring should not be decided by a machine. Each school should write and publish its own list of gated decisions.

crumbs.name: Ten Patterns That Show Up Everywhere

sections.body: This pattern places a person at the point where a consequential decision is made. AI can provide information, but it cannot make the call. The problem it solves is that some school decisions carry serious consequences for students, families, and staff, so they need human judgment and accountability. The text says every school should create its own version of the list and make it public. The list from Chapter 1 includes grades, special education services, discipline, course placement, teacher evaluation, safety flags, and hiring.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In early grades, the gate usually stands before screening, so a reading screener might flag a kindergartner as at risk for dyslexia, but a teacher and specialist review the child before any decision or communication with the family. In middle school, the gate often protects grades, because AI can suggest a quiz score but cannot post it. In high school, the gate matters most for discipline, where an AI detection score is never proof that a student cheated. The text gives these grade-band examples as the places where the gate most often applies. The common action is that a person must decide after reviewing the evidence.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text does not give an evidence label for this pattern. It cites research on human review warning that when a machine makes the first call, people tend to go along with it, even when it is wrong (Krugel et al., 2023). The fix described is for the person to look at the evidence first and treat the AI suggestion as a second opinion. Chapter 3 turns this into a written rule with a list of decisions every board can adopt. No other study, figure, or finding is provided in the supplied text.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The gate only works if the person behind it forms a real opinion, so passive approval is a risk. The text warns that people may defer to a machine's first call even when it is wrong. To guard against that, the person should examine the evidence before considering the AI suggestion, which then serves only as a second opinion. Decisions behind the gate stay with a person, and AI is never allowed to make them. The school should write its own list of gated decisions and publish it.
